blocks.text: Reading machine learning papers
An interactive reading sample · 2026
Abstract. Explore equations, figures, tables, and text selection in this offline sample. It is not a published research paper.
1. Start with the question

A useful first pass identifies the problem, the proposed method, and the evidence. Separate the authors’ claims from the measurements that support them. Mark passages that depend on assumptions you want to revisit.
Select a few words in this paragraph. The reader offers Copy, Explain in Chat, and Save snippet; a chat started from the passage stays connected to it.

An input x_i and a prediction \hat{y}_i are small parts of a larger argument. Seeing x_i again should preserve the same meaning while giving each occurrence its own reading anchor. The literal price $5 and the code $not_math$ are not equations.
2. Read the equations in context
Scaled dot-product attention turns compatibility scores between queries and keys into weights on values. Inspect each dimension before tracing how the expression fits into the model.
\begin{equation}\label{eq:attention} \operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V \end{equation}

The normalization in Equation (1) matters because the scale of raw compatibility scores changes with the key dimension. A contextual explanation should connect the equation to its surrounding argument. Tap the equation for Chat about Equation, Focus, or Copy as Text.

Queries and keys produce attention weights; those weights combine values into an output. Figure 1. A simplified attention data flow. Queries and keys are shown above values; both paths meet at the output. Tap the figure to inspect it, then return to the same place in the paper.
An aligned derivation makes intermediate assumptions visible:
\begin{align} s_{ij} &= \frac{q_i^{\mathsf T}k_j}{\sqrt{d_k}},\\ a_{ij} &= \frac{\exp(s_{ij})}{\sum_{r=1}^{n}\exp(s_{ir})},\\ o_i &= \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}v_j. \end{align}
A small matrix is easier to inspect than a long list of coefficients:
These numbers illustrate layout and row normalization; they are not measurements from a trained model.
3. Check the evaluation
Use tables to compare the conditions as well as the headline score. The example below is a layout fixture with illustrative labels, not experimental results.[1]

Condition Training data Compute held fixed? Uncertainty reported? Reading question Baseline Same split Yes Multiple seeds Is the reference competitive? Proposed method Same split Verify Check intervals Which change explains the gain? Ablation Same split Verify Check variance Does the component matter?
Keep the objective next to the results rather than treating a single score as the whole story:
\mathcal L(\theta)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\bigl(f_\theta(x_i)-y_i\bigr)^2+\lambda\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2.
Compare the same data split and measurement protocol. Check variation across runs, not only the best run. Read an ablation as evidence about a component, not proof of every claim.

Data is passed through a model and then checked across several runs. Figure 2. A reading checklist separates the data, the model, and the checks. The repeated bars represent repeated runs, not measured scores. This second diagram has its own figure and asset identity.
4. Follow the references

Follow relevant source papers without losing your current reading position. Tapping a reference opens its menu: copy it, open it on arXiv, add it to your library, or discuss it in chat. Eligible shared conversions can be reused, while your conversations and personal annotations remain private.
Offline check. This document, its equations, and its figure are bundled with the app. They require no network connection.
References

This original fixture describes familiar reading techniques and uses standard attention and squared-error expressions for rendering tests. It contains no reported benchmark results and is not an OCR output or a third-party paper.
A reading checklist can help compare papers, but it cannot replace checking the original experimental setup. ↩︎
